theory.overview: Greedy algorithms make locally optimal choices at each step with the hope of finding a global optimum. They are efficient and often produce optimal solutions for specific problems. However, greedy doesn't always work - proof of correctness is essential. Common applications include: Activity Selection (pick earliest finishing), Huffman Coding (merge lowest frequencies), Fractional Knapsack (take highest value/weight), and Minimum Spanning Tree (Kruskal's/Prim's).

keyConcepts.name: Greedy Choice Property
keyConcepts.description: A global optimum can be reached by choosing local optima at each step. The choice is made and never reconsidered.

keyConcepts.name: Optimal Substructure
keyConcepts.description: An optimal solution to the problem contains optimal solutions to subproblems. Like DP, but we only need one choice.

keyConcepts.name: Exchange Argument
keyConcepts.description: Proof technique: show any optimal solution can be transformed into the greedy solution without worsening it.

keyConcepts.name: When Greedy Fails
keyConcepts.description: 0/1 Knapsack, Longest Path, Set Cover - these require DP or backtracking. Always verify greedy works!
